'''Francisco Chíguil Figueroa'''{{Family name footnote|Chíguil|[[Figueroa]]|lang=Spanish}} (born 4 October 1961) is a Mexican economist, chemical engineer, and politician. A member of the [[National Regeneration Movement]] (Morena) who previously belonged to the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD), since 8 October 2024 he represents [[Mexico City]] in the [[Senate of Mexico|Senate]]. 

He previously served two terms in the [[Legislative Assembly of the Federal District]] and was elected to three terms as the borough chief (later: mayor) of [[Gustavo A. Madero, Mexico City]]. 

==Political career==
Francisco Chíguil was born on 4 October 1961 in [[San Andrés Tuxtla, Veracruz]]. He holds a bachelor's degree in chemical engineering from the [[National Polytechnic Institute]] (IPN) and a bachelor's and a master's in economics from the [[Metropolitan Autonomous University]] (UAM). In 2015 he completed a doctorate in economics at the IPN.<ref name=sil>{{cite web |title=Perfil: Sen. Francisco Chíguil Figueroa, LXVI Legislatura |publisher=[[Secretariat of the Interior|SEGOB]] |website=Sistema de Información Legislativa (SIL) |url=https://sil.gobernacion.gob.mx/Librerias/pp_PerfilLegislador.php?Referencia=9228911 |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref>

His political career began in 1997 when he was elected to a three-year term in the [[Legislative Assembly of the Federal District]] (ALDF) for the [[Party of the Democratic Revolution]] (PRD). In 2000, Gustavo A. Madero borough chief {{ill|Joel Ortega Cuevas|es}} appointed him executive director of economic development in the borough. In 2003 he was elected to a second term in the ALDF.<ref name=sil/>

In 2006, on the PRD ticket, he was elected borough chief of Gustavo A. Madero for the 2006–2008 term.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.aldf.gob.mx/archivo-50fb2adaf0c30b4529241e20071e25be.pdf |title=Diario de los Debates de la Asamblea Legislativa del Distrito Federal |date=7 December 2006 |publisher=[[Asamblea Legislativa del Distrito Federal|ALDF]] |pages=3-10 |format=pdf}}</ref>
He resigned his position on 25 June 2008 following a [[New's Divine nightclub tragedy|human stampede at the New's Divine nightclub]] in which 12 people were killed.<ref>{{cite news |title=Acepta Ebrard separación de Chíguil de su cargo |trans-title=Ebrard accepts Chíguil's resignation | url=http://www.eluniversal.com.mx/notas/517789.html |work=[[El Universal (Mexico)|El Universal]] |date=25 June 2008 |archive-date=22 May 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090522010351/https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/notas/517789.html}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=¿Dónde están hoy los políticos involucrados en el caso News Divine? |trans-title=Where are the politicians involved in the News Divine case now? |url=https://politica.expansion.mx/cdmx/2019/06/20/donde-estan-hoy-los-politicos-involucrados-en-el-caso-news-divine |work=[[Expansión (Mexico)|Expansión]] |date=20 June 2019}}</ref>

In 2018, as a member of the [[National Regeneration Movement]] (Morena), he was elected mayor of Gustavo A. Madero, and he was re-elected for a second consecutive term in 2021.<ref name=sil/> 

He took a leave of absence from his position as mayor in October 2023 in the run-up to the [[2024 Mexican local election|2024 elections]] to coordinate [[Clara Brugada]]'s successful campaign for election as [[Head of Government of Mexico City|head of government of Mexico City]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Francisco Chíguil se suma a Brugada: el alcalde de GAM pide licencia para convertirse en jefe de campaña |trans-title=Francisco Chíguil joins Brugada: GAM mayor requests leave of absence to serve as campaign chief |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/elecciones/francisco-chiguil-se-suma-a-brugada-el-alcalde-de-gam-pide-licencia-para-convertirse-en-jefe-de-campana/ |work=[[El Universal (Mexico)|El Universal]] |date=7 October 2023}}</ref>
At the same time, his name appeared on the ballot for the [[2024 Mexican Senate election|Senate election]], as the [[Legislator#Substitute legislator|alternate]] of [[Omar García Harfuch]], the lead candidate of the ''[[Sigamos Haciendo Historia]]'' coalition in Mexico City.<ref>{{cite web |title=Candidatos y candidatas |url=https://candidaturas.ine.mx/ |website=Senadurías mayoría relativa: Ciudad de México |publisher=[[National Electoral Institute|INE]] |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Tapia Sandoval |first=Anayeli |date=4 June 2024 |title=Resultados electorales: ¿Qué pasó con las candidaturas de Omar García Harfuch y Sandra Cuevas? |trans-title=Electoral results: What happened with the candidacies of Omar García Harfuch and Sandra Cuevas? |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/06/04/resultados-electorales-que-paso-con-las-candidaturas-de-omar-garcia-harfuch-y-sandra-cuevas/ |work=Infobae}}</ref>

''Sigamos Haciendo Historia'' won the election in the capital and García Harfuch was duly elected to Mexico City's first Senate seat.<ref>{{cite web |title=Senadurías: Ciudad de México |url=https://computos2024.ine.mx/senadurias/nacional/entidad/9/candidatura |website=Cómputos Distritales 2024 |publisher=[[National Electoral Institute|INE]] |access-date=20 December 2025}}</ref>
However, President-elect [[Claudia Sheinbaum]] had previously announced that García Harfuch was to serve in her cabinet as [[Secretariat of Security and Citizen Protection|secretary of security and citizen protection]] and, as his alternate, Chíguil Figueroa was sworn in his stead on 8 October 2024.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Vargas |first1=Octavio |title=Quién suplirá a Omar García Harfuch en el Senado tras nombramiento como Secretario de Seguridad por Sheinbaum |trans-title=Who will replace Omar García Harfuch in the Senate after his appointment as security secretary? |url=https://www.infobae.com/mexico/2024/07/04/quien-suplira-a-omar-garcia-harfuch-en-el-senado-tras-nombramiento-como-secretario-de-seguridad-por-sheinbaum/ |website=Infobae |access-date=5 July 2024 |date=4 July 2024}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Karen Castrejón, María Guadalupe Chavira y Francisco Chíguil rinden protesta como senadores de la República |trans-title=Karen Castrejón, María Guadalupe Chavira and Francisco Chíguil sworn in as senators |url=https://comunicacionsocial.senado.gob.mx/informacion/comunicados/9825-karen-castrejon-maria-guadalupe-chavira-y-francisco-chiguil-rinden-protesta-como-senadores-de-la-republica |work=Comunicación social |publisher=[[Senate (Mexico)|Senado de la República]] |date=8 October 2024}}</ref>

In the Senate, he serves on the standing committees for migratory affairs, economic development and entrepreneurship, and parliamentary rules and procedure.<ref>{{cite web |title=Chíguil Figueroa, Francisco |url=https://morena.senado.gob.mx/francisco-chiguil-figueroa/ |website=Senadores Morena, LXVI Legislatura |publisher=[[Senate (Mexico)|Senado de la República]] |access-date=21 December 2025}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Francisco Chíguil is married to fellow politician [[Beatriz Rojas Martínez]].<ref>{{cite news |title=La pareja imperial que busca la alcaldía de GAM |url=https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/metropoli/la-pareja-imperial-que-busca-la-alcaldia-de-gam/ |trans-title=The imperial couple seeking the GAM mayoralty |work=[[El Universal (Mexico)|El Universal]] |date=7 December 2020}}</ref>
